results.criterion: 1. One HTML file, inline CSS and JS, no build step
results.note: One <style> block and one <script> block. The only external reference is the Google Fonts <link>, which is a CDN and allowed. Each visitor's browser contacts Google Fonts, but no form data is involved.

results.criterion: 2. Five sections, each reachable from visible nav
results.note: <nav aria-label="Main"> links #home, #book, #emergency, #doctors and #blog. Matching section ids exist for all five.

results.criterion: 3. Booking form opens a WhatsApp or tel: link; no external form service, no storage
results.note: <form id="bookForm"> has no action. The submit handler uses window.open("https://wa.me/...") and window.location.href="tel:"+num. A search of the source found no fetch(, XMLHttpRequest, localStorage, sessionStorage or document.cookie. Warning: CFG holds PLACEHOLDER_* tokens, and the regex /^\+?\d{8,15}$/ rejects them, so today the buttons only show #notice. The link-opening path was read but not executed.

results.criterion: 4. Plain text says the hospital confirms by phone and live slots are not offered
results.note: en book_note: "The hospital confirms your slot by phone. Live slots are not offered." Kannada and Hindi equivalents are present.

results.criterion: 5. Emergency number and address as marked placeholders, short numeric layout
results.note:
em_num "[[emergency number]]" renders in

as [PLACEHOLDER: ...]. em_addr is likewise marked. There are 3 short steps and 1 warning line. No digits are invented.

results.criterion: 6. Doctor cards fully placeholder
results.note: 4 cards built from d_name, d_spec, d_cred and d_photo, all [[...]] tokens. doc_note: "All profiles below are placeholders."

results.criterion: 7. Blog posts placeholder, no medical claims
results.note: 3 cards from p_title, p_date and p_sum, all [[...]]. blog_note: "Posts are placeholders. Nothing here is medical advice."

results.criterion: 8. Language switch EN/KN/HI; every section has KN and HI text
results.note: Buttons data-l=en, kn and hi. I counted 51 keys in the en dictionary and found the same key set in kn and hi by reading, not by running code. Every data-i18n key used in the markup has a kn and hi entry.

results.criterion: 9. Every KN and HI view shows 'pending native review'
results.note: setLang sets #rev.hidden=(l==="en"). The kn and hi rev_banner strings both contain "pending native review". The Kannada and Hindi emergency columns also carry a class="rev" line. Visible rendering was not checked in a browser.

results.criterion: 10. Emergency English text beside Kannada and Hindi
results.note: Three .col blocks with data-fix=en, kn and hi sit in .cols{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)}. @media(max-width:800px){.cols{grid-template-columns:1fr}} stacks them on narrow screens. English still comes first in the same section, but it is not side by side. Many patients will use phones, so this is worth a decision. A cheaper fix is a two-column layout with English on top and the translation next to it.

results.criterion: 11. One consistent placeholder marker; no unmarked phone number or address
results.note: ph() turns every [[x]] into [PLACEHOLDER: x], including in the Kannada and Hindi strings. The source has no phone-length digit sequence and no street address. The tel/WhatsApp targets are the tokens PLACEHOLDER_WHATSAPP_NUMBER and PLACEHOLDER_CALLBACK_NUMBER, which the criterion allows.
